nri-world.title: The U.S. Just Told Green Card Applicants to Leave the Country and Apply From Home. For Hundreds of Thousands of Indians, the Nightmare Scenario Is Here.

For the estimated 400,000 Indians with pending green card applications, the policy means leaving jobs, separating from families, and entering a consular backlog that stretches years.

nri-world.nri_angle: Indians are the single largest nationality in the U.S. employment-based green card backlog, with wait times that already stretch decades due to per-country caps. This policy change forces them to choose between staying in the U.S. on temporary visas — with no path to permanence — or leaving their jobs, homes, and children's schools to apply from India, where U.S. consular wait times in Mumbai and Delhi already exceed 18 months.

markets-finance.title: India Wants Your Dollars. The RBI Is Dusting Off the 2013 Playbook — NRI Bonds, FCNR Deposits, Emergency Swaps — to Stop the Rupee From Hitting 100. If You Have a Dollar Account, You Are About to Be Courted.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India conducted a $5 billion dollar-rupee swap auction on May 26, 2026 — the same day the rupee was trading near its record low of 96.96 per dollar. But the swap is only one weapon in an escalating arsenal. Sources familiar with the central bank's thinking told multiple outlets that the RBI is actively evaluating the launch of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) deposit schemes, the issuance of NRI bonds, and additional swap operations to mobilise dollar inflows from the Indian diaspora. The last time India took these steps was during the 2013 taper tantrum crisis, when the rupee fell to 68.85 against the dollar and the RBI raised $34 billion from NRIs in three months through FCNR-B deposits offered at subsidised rates. That 2013 operation is widely credited with stabilising the currency and averting a balance-of-payments crisis. India's current predicament is arguably worse: the Iran war has pushed Brent crude above $100 per barrel, foreign portfolio investors have sold $23 billion of Indian equities in 2026, the rupee has fallen 6 percent since January, the RBI is spending an estimated $1 billion per day in the spot market to prevent further collapse, and fuel prices have been hiked four times in May alone — a cumulative increase of ₹7.5 per litre. For the estimated 32 million members of the Indian diaspora — particularly the 4.5 million Indian Americans who hold dollar-denominated savings, earn dollar salaries, and send an estimated $30 billion in remittances to India each year — the coming weeks may present a once-in-a-decade financial decision. The RBI is about to ask you for your dollars. Understanding what FCNR deposits are, how the 2013 scheme worked, what the current remittance and property arbitrage looks like, and whether parking your dollars in India makes financial sense requires more than a headline. It requires context.

technology.excerpt: Product teams, ad sales, and marketing roles hit across India as Meta spends $145 billion on AI and asks whether it even knows how many humans it needs.
technology.nri_angle: Indian professionals at Meta — both in India and on H-1B in the US — face an uncertain future as the company flattens hierarchies and redirects resources to AI. H-1B holders get 60 days to find new work or leave the country.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Developer Army Hits 27 Million. The West Should Pay Attention.
technology.excerpt: India now adds one in seven new developers globally, leads open-source AI contributions, and is on track to overtake the US by 2030. The talent pipeline that built Silicon Valley is being replicated at home.
technology.nri_angle: The talent pipeline NRIs once represented — IIT grads heading west on H-1B — is being replicated at massive scale inside India. For diaspora professionals, it is both validation and competition for the career moat they built by moving West.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Jensen Huang Calls AI Layoff Excuses 'Lazy.' He Has a Point.
technology.excerpt: The Nvidia CEO says companies blaming AI for job cuts are covering for bad strategy. For Indian tech workers caught in the crossfire, his argument matters.
technology.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals on H-1B are disproportionately concentrated at the companies doing the cutting. Huang's counter-narrative — that AI should create more jobs, not fewer — offers both reassurance and a challenge to upskill.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's $100 Billion GCC Engine Is Being Rewritten by AI
technology.excerpt: Salary inflation of 50 per cent, an 'India plus' hedging strategy, and AI-driven headcount compression are transforming the model that employs 2.36 million people.
technology.nri_angle: GCC transformation directly reshapes the return-to-India calculus for NRI tech workers — senior roles now carry real authority and narrowing pay gaps, while AI threatens entry-level hiring pipelines.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nvidia Will Spend $150 Billion a Year in Taiwan. Where Does That Leave India?
technology.excerpt: Jensen Huang's massive bet on Taipei as the AI manufacturing capital underscores the distance India must travel in its own semiconductor ambitions.
technology.nri_angle: Nvidia's Taiwan consolidation affects tens of thousands of Indian-origin chip engineers in the US while highlighting the gap between India's nascent fab ambitions and Taiwan's entrenched dominance.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Micron Crosses $1 Trillion as Sanjay Mehrotra Joins the Rarefied Club
technology.excerpt: The Indian-American CEO's memory chip empire has tripled in value this year, fuelled by insatiable AI demand and a $2.75 billion Gujarat fab now in production.
technology.nri_angle: Indian-American CEO leads memory chip giant to $1 trillion valuation; Gujarat semiconductor plant marks India's first real entry into the global chip supply chain, creating opportunities for NRI engineers and investors.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: JioHotstar Just Put ₹4,000 Crore on South India. After Bollywood's Worst May in Five Years, the Math Makes Sense.
entertainment.excerpt: 1,500 hours of new Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam content. Kerala Crime Files returns. Vijay Sethupathi and Nivin Pauly sign on. The biggest bet in Indian OTT history follows the money to where the audiences actually are.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Triptii Dimri Was a Background in a Bathtub Two Years Ago. She Now Has Four Films Opposite Prabhas, Madhuri Dixit, and Ranbir Kapoor.
entertainment.excerpt: From Animal's breakout moment to a ₹1,000-crore slate spanning Spirit, Maa Behen, Animal Park, and a Parveen Babi biopic — the fastest career acceleration in recent Bollywood history.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: A Song From a Film That Flopped in 2015 Just Became the Most-Streamed Indian Track on Spotify. It Has 717 Million Plays.
entertainment.excerpt: 'Agar Tum Saath Ho' from Tamasha overtakes 'Kesariya' — composed by A.R. Rahman, sung by Arijit Singh and Alka Yagnik, the track is now Indian music's defining digital monument.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Aamir Khan Says a Film Flopping Feels Like Losing a Child. His Son's Film Just Made ₹5.44 Crore. He Produced It.
entertainment.excerpt: Ek Din opened advance bookings 39 days early — a Bollywood record. It starred Sai Pallavi in her Hindi debut. It earned ₹1 crore on day one. Aamir says he goes into depression for two to three months after every flop. This one had his son's name on it.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Kangana Ranaut Defended Aishwarya Rai at Cannes. These Two Women Have Spent a Decade Being Pitted Against Each Other. The Internet Had No Script for This.
entertainment.excerpt: Aishwarya walked the Cannes red carpet for the 24th time. Trolls mocked her appearance. Kangana posted an Instagram Story calling her 'glorious' and told critics to get used to seeing older women. Bollywood's most unlikely alliance just happened.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Bollywood's Oldest Film Union Just Told Ranveer Singh No One Will Work With Him. He Succeeded Shah Rukh Khan as Don. Now He Can't Make a Film.
entertainment.excerpt: FWICE issues a non-cooperation directive after Ranveer walked out of Don 3 three weeks before the shoot. Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani claim ₹45 crore in pre-production losses. The actor offered ₹35 crore. They said no.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: South Indian Theatres Just Told Netflix to Wait Eight Weeks. If You Live Abroad, This Is About You.
entertainment.excerpt: A new exhibitor mandate across Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam cinema forces an 8-week theatrical window before any OTT release. For the diaspora, it means waiting two months for every South Indian film that doesn't get a global day-and-date release.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ram Charan Broke His Leg for RRR. For Peddi, He Can't Lift His Daughter. The Biggest Indian Film of June Opens in Seven Days.
entertainment.excerpt: A.R. Rahman's soundtrack just debuted on the US charts. The runtime is 3 hours 9 minutes. Advance bookings in North America have already crossed $375,000. And the man at the centre of it says he might need an X-ray.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months to Play a God. Ranveer Singh Is Killing Zombies. Bollywood's 2027 War Just Started.
entertainment.excerpt: Mahavatar is a Parashurama epic directed by the man who made Stree. Pralay is India's first zombie action film. Both are insane bets on a genre Bollywood has never cracked.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Nicolas Cage Is 62 and He Just Became Spider-Man. It Is the Best Thing on Prime Video This Week.
entertainment.excerpt: Spider-Noir drops on Prime Video in black-and-white and colour. The reviews are strong. The concept is absurd. It works.

entertainment.excerpt: Mohanlal's franchise closer earned more overseas than domestically in its first week — a rare feat that reveals where Malayalam cinema's real audience lives.

lifestyle-health.title: A 19-Year Study of 20,000 Adults Found That the Type of Sitting Matters More Than the Amount. Mentally Active Sitting Cuts Dementia Risk. Passive Sitting Raises It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers tracked sedentary behaviour for nearly two decades and found that replacing one hour of TV-watching with reading or puzzles was associated with a significant reduction in dementia risk. For Indian tech workers who sit 10 hours a day and come home to Netflix, the distinction is not academic.

sources.label: Frontiers in Public Health — Sedentary Behaviour and Burnout

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Asian Americans Have the Lowest Rate of Anxiety Medication Use in the Country. A National Study of 29,000 Adults Found That Cultural Stigma Is Only Part of the Explanation.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A May 2026 Frontiers study found that even after controlling for income, insurance, and education, Asian adults had 45 per cent lower odds of taking anxiety medication than White adults. For South Asian families where mental health is still discussed in whispers, the treatment gap is likely even wider.

sources.label: Emory University — South Asian Women Mental Health

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 100,000 People Found That Food Dyes Raise Diabetes Risk by 38 Per Cent and Cancer Risk by 14 Per Cent. Your Grandmother's Kitchen Did Not Use a Single One of Them.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The NutriNet-Santé cohort study is the first to link colour additives to chronic disease at scale. Curcumin as an additive — not as turmeric — was the worst offender.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Turmeric in whole-food form offers anti-inflammatory benefits. As an isolated food additive, it was linked to a 49 per cent increase in diabetes risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Diabetes Drug Millions of South Asians Already Take May Be Quietly Slowing Their Cancer. A Cleveland Clinic Study of 12,112 Patients Found the Evidence.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic cut cancer progression by up to 55 per cent across four tumour types. South Asians, who carry the world's highest diabetes burden, may be benefiting without knowing it.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for diabetes, are showing unexpected cancer-protective properties
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 17,000 Adults Found You Need Four Times More Exercise Than the Guidelines Recommend. The 150-Minute Rule Is a Floor, Not a Ceiling.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at Macao Polytechnic University found that 560 to 610 minutes of weekly aerobic exercise — about 85 minutes a day — reduced cardiovascular events by more than 30 per cent. The standard 150-minute guideline cut risk by only 8 per cent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The American Heart Association Just Rewrote Its Dietary Rules. Your Mother's Indian Kitchen Already Follows Most of Them.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The 2026 AHA guidelines prioritise plant proteins over meat, push potassium and whole grains, and take a harder line on alcohol. Traditional Indian cooking checks nearly every box — except the one about salt.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Parents' Three-Meals-a-Day Habit Was Protecting Their Muscles. A Study Found That Eating Fewer Than Three Meals Is Independently Linked to Lower Muscle Mass — Regardless of How Much Protein You Eat.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Korean study adds to mounting evidence that meal frequency matters as much as total intake for preserving skeletal muscle. For Indian families watching their elders skip meals to manage blood sugar, the implications are urgent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Sixty-One Per Cent of Asian Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Already Show Early Muscle Loss. South Asians Are the Most Vulnerable Group. Your Parents May Not Know They Have It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new meta-analysis of 14 studies across Asia found that sarcopenia begins years before diabetes patients notice it — and the vegetarian diets many Indian families follow may be accelerating the decline.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One Hour of Recovery Sleep After a Bad Night Erases the Mortality Signal. A Study of 574,000 Nights Proves Your Body Knows What It Needs — If You Let It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tsinghua University researchers tracked 85,000 people with wrist-worn devices. Those who slept one extra hour after sleep deprivation had the same mortality risk as those who never lost sleep at all.

sources.label: Dr. Jean-Philippe Chaput, University of Ottawa

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRI professionals routinely grind through sleep-deprived weekdays with no recovery signal. This study shows the body can self-repair after a bad night — but only if the alarm clock and caffeine do not override it.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Sleep Window That Slows Aging Is Narrower Than You Think. A Study of 500,000 People Found It. Most Indian Tech Workers Are Outside It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Columbia University study published in Nature mapped 23 biological aging clocks against sleep duration. The optimal range is 6.4 to 7.8 hours — and both extremes accelerate cellular aging.

sources.label: Fox News Digital (Dr. Saema Tahir interview)

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian tech workers in the US routinely sleep under six hours, layering a modifiable aging accelerant on top of the elevated cardiovascular and metabolic risk already documented in South Asians.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Doctor Uses a BMI of 25 to Decide Whether to Screen You for Diabetes. For South Asians, the Correct Number Is 20. A Harvard-Led Study Says the Current Threshold Is Missing Millions.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A cross-sectional analysis of NHANES data found that a 35-year-old Asian American at BMI 25 already has nearly triple the diabetes prevalence of a White American at the same weight. The screening system was never designed for your body.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India's Deadliest Heatwave in a Decade Has Killed at Least 77 People. Modi Just Warned the Nation. If You Are Planning a Summer Trip Home, You Need a Different Playbook.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Temperatures have crossed 47°C in central India. Telangana alone has lost 52 people. Unofficial counts suggest 200 to 300 more. The India your parents describe from May is not the India that exists in May 2026.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Salesforce's Agentforce Hit $1.2 Billion. Indian IT Services Should Be Worried.
carousel.excerpt: The CRM giant beat earnings estimates but its AI agent platform threatens the consulting-heavy model that employs hundreds of thousands of Indians globally.
carousel.image_caption: A modern tech workspace — the kind of environment where Salesforce's AI agents may soon replace human consultants.
carousel.nri_angle: Salesforce is among the top H-1B employers in the US, and Indian IT services firms like TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCL derive billions from Salesforce consulting and implementation. The rise of Agentforce — AI agents that automate CRM workflows — directly threatens this labor-intensive model. For Indian-origin Salesforce developers, consultants, and IT services investors, this earnings report is a weather vane.
